notes: Line labels L01–L24 count the 24 full-width typed prose lines, excluding the two diagram rows, interlinear additions and four slanting margin-note lines. D1 is the large square; D2 is the small handwritten square; M1–M4 label the marginal note. The sheet has no separate authorial page number; archive 18 is a comment only.

The page continues the Kostant/Dynkin discussion, compares Dyn_c, ST_c, Un_c and the underlined slashed-ring object through homogeneous-space diagrams, and discusses rational parabolics, rational Dynkin data, arithmetic questions and filtrations from unipotents. These are source assertions, not conclusions proved by this transcription.

The upper-right square’s apparent stabilizer interpretation makes a group Z(e) mathematically plausible, while the lower-right ink is 3-shaped with a returning loop. This contextual tension prompted a full-square relook and remains a doubt, not a reason to replace the written glyph.
The non-inner-form caveat is explicit: one must first verify that the class c′ of P comes from a Dynkin c invariant under Γ. The text does not claim that this verification has been completed.

The source expressly says that invariance of c does not clearly follow from invariance of c′, faute de savoir si c↦c′ est injectif sur les classes de Dynkin. The insertion de c is preserved at propriété. No injectivity theorem is supplied editorially.

The marginal note reads Il n’est en effet pas le cas, p.ex. pour A_2,A_4 (cela l’est pour A_3). Its grammatical reference is not resolved, and the A-type examples have not been independently proved here.

The semi-local-ring extension is qualified exactly as written by de car. nulle jusqu’à nouvel ordre. It remains a provisional restriction, not an unconditional statement over arbitrary characteristic.

The stabilizer comparison is presented as a question to investigate: de voir si: leur stabilisateur dans Autext(G_o) est le même … et pas str. plus grand. The unexpected colon and str. abbreviation are retained.

The agreement de cette classe rationnel is retained. The overworked final letter in invariante and the pen stroke within parab-oliques are retained with in-place doubts; neither grammar nor mathematical expectation repairs them.
The final printed der- ends the leaf. Under the inherited line-end joining convention the draft retains der% without a lexical hyphen; crop26 records the visible hyphen. No next leaf was consulted.

H’s explanatory note about the small square is editorial and is not ink. Macro-only differences, including handwritten wrappers, operatorname versus mathrm, colon spacing, ampersand syntax and archive/page markers, have no change rows.

The two first application signs were checked independently: the first terminates in a flat stub, the second in a pointed right tip. Later c↦c′ has a clear pointed head. No arrow was inferred merely by repetition.

check_events.outcome: Conditional local check only: over an infinite field k, a nonempty k-defined Zariski-open subset of affine n-space has a k-point. It contains D(f) for a nonzero polynomial f, and induction on n gives a k-point where f is nonzero. This supports the source’s open-dense-vector-space step under those hypotheses; it does not establish the rational Levi, the open set’s definition or the semi-local extension.

Conditional elementary check: if the map of Γ-sets c↦c′ is equivariant and injective, Γ-invariance of c′ forces Γ-invariance of c, since c and γc have the same image. The page explicitly leaves injectivity and the required invariant lift unverified; neither premise is proved here.

reading_notes: The sheet continues the discussion of Kostant/Dynkin data. It compares Dyn_c, ST_c, Un_c and the underlined filtration-object glyph by a square of homogeneous-space maps; a smaller marginal square records the associated stabilizers. The lower-right marginal glyph looks like fraktur z(e), although a group Z(e) would suit the apparent stabilizer interpretation. That tension prompted reinspection and remains explicit in the transcription.

The main paragraph relates rational points of the filtration/parabolic object to rational Dynkin data and argues through a rational Levi subgroup and a dense open subset of g(2). A local conditional fact was checked: a nonempty k-defined open subset of affine space has a k-point if k is infinite. This does not establish the other premises or the semi-local-ring extension claimed on the sheet.

For a non-inner form the author says “il faut faire attention cependant de vérifier d’abord” that the parabolic class c′ lifts to a Γ-invariant Dynkin class c. He adds “il n’est pas clair que cette propriété” (with inserted “de c”) follows from invariance of c′, “faute de savoir si c↦c′ est injectif sur les classes de Dynkin”. The elementary implication for an injective equivariant map was checked conditionally; injectivity itself was not established.

The margin reads “Il n’est en effet pas le cas, p.ex. pour A₂,A₄ (cela l’est pour A₃)”. Its grammatical reference is not decided editorially and these A-type examples were not independently proved. The semi-local statement retains the author’s restriction “de car. nulle jusqu’à nouvel ordre”.

The arithmetic paragraph asks to determine the Dynkin–Kostant parabolic classes and to see whether their stabilizer in Autext(G_o) equals that of the corresponding Dynkin c, “et pas str. plus grand”. The unusual “si:” remains. The final paragraph begins a statement about the filtration and the conjugacy class of its defining unipotent, then ends mid-word at der-.

The first action sign has a bar and a shaft without a distinct arrowhead, whereas the second and c↦c′ have pointed heads. The insertion after au is a shorthand (= or an overlined m), not the written word même. Neither notation nor grammar was allowed to erase the overtyping, the doubtful final letter in invariante, or the stroke within parab-oliques.
